p: In the holy Torah is mentioned
שֵׁם הֶחָג הַזֶּה בְּשֵׁם חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת
the name of this festival as "Chag HaShavuos,"
שִׁבְעָה שָׁבוּעוֹת תִּסְפּוֹר לָךְ וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים טז, ט)
"Seven weeks shall you count for yourself," etc. (Devarim 16:9),
עַד מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת וְגוֹמֵר (וַיִּקְרָא כג, טז).
"until the morrow of the Shabbos," etc. (Vayikra 23:16).
That is, it is the source
שֶׁל הַשַּׁבָּתוֹת שֶׁל הַשִּׁבְעָה שָׁבוּעוֹת דִּסְפִירָה,
of the "Shabbosos" of the seven weeks of the counting,
and it is in essence the holiness of Shabbos.
For the holiness of the Shabbos day
of the six days of work,
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה׳ (שְׁמוֹת כ, יא).
And Chag HaShavuos is the all-encompassing Shabbos
Each week of the counting, too,
which shines into all the days of the week.
וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת (וַיִּקְרָא כג, טו).
We have already spoken of this:
that all the festivals and holy convocations
are called in the holy Torah by the name "Shabbason,"
such as "on the first day a Shabbason
and on the eighth day a Shabbason" (Vayikra 23:39);
וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שַׁבָּתוֹן זִכְרוֹן תְּרוּעָה (וַיִּקְרָא כג, כד),
on Rosh Hashanah, "a Shabbason, a remembrance of the teruah" (Vayikra 23:24);
וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן (וַיִּקְרָא כג, לב).
and on Yom Kippur, "a Shabbos of Shabbason" (Vayikra 23:32).
that comes from the arousal of man.
Therefore it is written with the diminutive nun,
which serves to diminish the matter,
like the nun of "ishon," the "little man" of the eye, as is known.
Except that for Chag HaMatzos and Chag HaShavuos
That is because on the day of the Exodus
there shines, in essence, the holiness of Shabbos
from Above, which is "fixed and established."
As they said about the "night of watching" (Shemos 12:42):
"guarded and coming since the six days of Creation"
which is not so with Shabbos,
upon the days of the coming week, as is known.
אָכֵן עַל יְדֵי הַסְּפִירַת שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת
But through the counting of seven Shabbosos
we come to the illumination of the holiness of the Shabbos
of the day of the Exodus.
only in connection with the mitzvah of the counting:
"And you shall count," etc., "from the morrow of the Shabbos."
And when we reach the fiftieth day,
there is included in it, in essence,
the totality of the Shabbos holiness
That is, the totality of the Shabbos holiness
of the totality of the seven sefiros,
and for this it is called Chag HaShavuos.
Now in the words of Chazal
נִקְרָא חַג הַזֶּה בְּשֵׁם חַג עֲצֶרֶת,
and this follows the allusion of the Midrash
that the day of Shemini Atzeres after Sukkos
with Chag HaShavuos that follows Pesach,
and it too would have been fitting to come
seven weeks after the festival of Sukkos,
וְהוּא כִּי עֲצֶרֶת הוּא לְשׁוֹן קְלִיטָה,
The point is that "Atzeres" is an expression of absorption,
meaning that there is absorbed in it
all the holiness of the festival, in the root;
and this is "It shall be an Atzeres for you."
שֶׁהוּא אַחַר שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת שֶׁל חַג הַפֶּסַח
which comes seven weeks after Chag HaPesach
and is the time of Mattan Torah —
שֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
which accords with the revelation of human comprehension
in the aspect of the seven holy revealed middos,
נִקְרָא עַל זֶה שֵׁם הֶחָג בְּשֵׁם שָׁבוּעוֹת,
like the shining of the aspect of Shabbos holiness
בְּשֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁל יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן.
in the seven holy middos of the days of building.
וְרַק עַל שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח נֶאֱמַר
Only about the seventh day of Pesach does it say
for then it is the aspect of absorption in the root,
and this is only "to Hashem your G-d,"
as is known from the holy Zohar that "it depends on Atika."
a flash of the light for the moment,
as our Sages of blessed memory said:
"A maidservant saw at the Sea," etc.
But at the time of Mattan Torah,
אָז בְּכֹחַ בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
then, by the power of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
they come to the binding to the root
שֶׁהָיָה הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כַּיָּדוּעַ:
who was the root of Torah she'b'al peh, as is known:
וְכָל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ (אִיּוֹב כח, י),
"And every precious thing his eye has seen" (Iyov 28:10) —
this is the eye of Rabbi Akiva;
things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues.
וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא בְּדִבְרֵי חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
Therefore in the words of Chazal,
in the Torah she'b'al peh, it is called "Atzeres,"
which is the aspect of absorption in the root
by the power of receiving the Torah she'b'al peh.
And so in the Torah she'b'al peh
like the matter of Shemini Atzeres:
"it shall be for you" — "for you" precisely.
